title: Planning Methods, Economics, Communication, Research Design, and Negotiation Foundations

sources.notes: MIT OCW Quantitative Reasoning and Statistical Methods for Planners I course identity for logical, empirically based arguments, statistics, probability, quantitative reasoning, description, estimation, comparison, explanation, planning practice limits, lecture notes, assignments, and exams.

MIT OCW quantitative reasoning syllabus identity for planning/design/policy quantitative information, sound reasoning, statistical methods, presentation and visualization of complex information, quantitative/qualitative method boundary, samples/populations, meaningful difference versus noise, recitations, assignments, lecture notes, and exams.

MIT OCW Planning Economics course identity for applying microeconomic theory to market failures and planning issues, global warming, public-good valuation, New York City development, city formation, location premiums, time-distributed costs/benefits, problem sets, exams, and solutions.

MIT OCW planning economics syllabus identity for microeconomics prerequisite, lecture/recitation/math-review format, graded problem sets, midterms, final exam, study groups, textbook boundary, and cost-benefit evaluation over time.

MIT OCW Research Design for Policy Analysis and Planning course identity for research-design skills, logic of the research process, social-science concepts, epistemological orientations, methodological techniques, planning specializations, seminar participation, and written assignments.

MIT OCW research-design syllabus identity for critical reflection, article summaries, participation, CNC and LG assignments, survey/interview/draft/final project stages, writing standards, and late-work boundaries.

MIT OCW Argumentation and Communication course identity for intensive writing workshop, cogent persuasive arguments, analytical frameworks, critical reading, effective writing, lecture notes, and written assignments.

MIT OCW communication syllabus identity for argument parts, memos, oral briefings, graphics critique, peer review, active listening, constructive feedback, Gateway assignment boundary, short assignments, presentations, and attendance.

MIT OCW Negotiation and Dispute Resolution in the Public Sector course identity for public-sector resource allocation and policy disputes, multi-party negotiation, dispute resolution, fairness/efficiency/stability/wisdom, lectures, scenarios, case studies, video analysis, role-play simulations, instructor insights, notes, and assignments.

MIT OCW negotiation syllabus identity for consensus building, collaboration, Program on Negotiation boundary, required texts, readings, role-play simulation exercises, reflection memos, videotaped negotiations, public-sector leadership, scenarios, and final exam boundary.
